D2/512MiB mechanism + long-duration trajectory diagnostic (no training; no new head-to-head)

PART A/B - D2 replication and mechanism
  replication pairs=20 v6 mean=31137.7ms aria2 mean=53452.1ms geo ratio=0.5816 range=[0.520,0.675] v6 faster=20/20
  established pooled: ratio=0.5816 CI=[0.5660384368857619, 0.5975357576204594] p=5e-06 claim_supported=True
  aria2 range sizes=[33554432]; v6 range sizes=[1048576]
  aria2 requests started <2s/2-4s/>=4s = {'<2s': 15, '2-4s': 0, '>=4s': 0}
  v6    requests started <2s/2-4s/>=4s = {'<2s': 2.95, '2-4s': 3.75, '>=4s': 505.3}
  mechanism: At 512 MiB aria2 splits into 16 pieces of 32 MiB (--split=16); each piece is one HTTP range request whose pacing rate is selected at request start and held for the whole request. All aria2 requests start before the 2 s transition at the 640 KiB/s initial rate, so ~32 MiB/request at 640 KiB/s takes ~51 s. v6 allocates 1 MiB ranges dynamically, so its requests complete in ~1.6 s and 505/512 are issued after recovery at 2.5 MiB/s. The reversal is therefore a request-granularity x phase-locked-pacing interaction, not evidence of generic adaptive superiority.
